issues.legal_issue: A pre-cutoff gallantry grant remains eligible for the statutory exemption when the grant was made to an awardee but, following the awardee’s death, the land was allotted to an heir, provided the statutory holding and transfer conditions are met.
material_facts: Land was granted in 1946 for the gallantry of a member of the armed forces who had died during the war.
After the grant was made posthumously, the land was allotted in the name of the awardee’s male-line descendant.
The descendant took possession of the granted land.
issues.conclusion: The grant was to the awardee, not to the heir merely because the posthumous allotment was made in the heir’s name. Land granted for gallantry before the cutoff date is excluded from surplus-area computation, and a tenant has no right to purchase it, while it is held by the grantee or a qualifying successor and has not passed through more than three successive hands by inheritance or bequest.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19DD of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, inserted by Punjab Act No. 12 of 1968 with retrospective effect, provides the exemption for qualifying pre-cutoff gallantry grants. Section 18 provides the tenant’s purchase mechanism, which section 19DD excludes for such land. The Court relied on the terms of the grant and the government instructions that posthumous allotments were to be made to the deceased grantee’s male-line descendants. No earlier cases were cited.

rule.if: gallantry_grant_proceeding and grant_made_before_cutoff and posthumous_award_allotment_to_heir and land_held_by_grantee_or_qualifying_successor and not passed_through_more_than_three_successive_inheritances_or_bequests

predicates.gallantry_grant_proceeding: The dispute concerns land granted in recognition of an armed-forces member’s gallantry.
predicates.grant_made_before_cutoff: The gallantry grant was made before the applicable cutoff date.
predicates.posthumous_award_allotment_to_heir: After the awardee died, the government allotted the granted land to an heir under the applicable posthumous-allotment arrangement.
predicates.land_held_by_grantee_or_qualifying_succe: The land is held by the original grantee or by a person succeeding to the land in a manner covered by the exemption.
predicates.passed_through_more_than_three_successiv: The land passed from the original grantee through more than three successive hands by inheritance or bequest.

issues.definition: When a qualifying pre-cutoff gallantry grant is allotted to an heir after the grantee’s death and remains within the specified holding and transfer limits, the original grant land is excluded from surplus computation and cannot be purchased by a tenant.

issues.legal_issue: Land allotted as compensation for gallantry-grant land lost after partition does not acquire the exemption attached to the original granted land merely because it compensates for that loss.
material_facts: The original gallantry-grant land was in territory left behind after partition.
The family migrated to India, where the government allotted different land as compensation for the land left behind.
The respondent possessed part of the compensation land as a tenant and obtained permission to purchase it under the tenancy law.
The appellant sought possession of the compensation land, asserting that it inherited the original land’s gallantry exemption.
The Court was shown no provision in the displaced-persons compensation legislation that transferred the exemption to replacement land.
issues.conclusion: The compensation land was not exempt from the tenant-purchase provisions on the ground that it replaced the original gallantry-grant land; the respondent’s purchase right therefore prevailed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 19DD of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, exempts qualifying gallantry-grant land, but the Court found no basis for extending that exemption to different land allotted as compensation. The Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954, contained no provision shown to transfer the exemption to compensation land. Section 18 was therefore not displaced on that basis. No earlier cases were cited.

predicates.tenant_purchase_dispute: The proceeding concerns a tenant’s claimed right to purchase land.
predicates.land_sought_is_compensation_for_lost_gal: The land sought to be purchased was allotted to compensate for gallantry-grant land that was lost.
predicates.land_sought_is_not_the_original_gallantr: The land sought to be purchased is different land from the original gallantry grant.
predicates.compensation_scheme_does_not_transfer_th: The compensation arrangement contains no term transferring the original land’s exemption to replacement land.

issues.definition: When a tenant seeks to purchase replacement land allotted as compensation, and the compensation arrangement does not transfer the exemption from the different original land, the replacement land is not exempt on that basis.

issues.legal_issue: When both sides claim equity and their equities are equal, the established legal right to purchase prevails.
material_facts: The appellant claimed that equity favored retaining the compensation land because it replaced land lost after partition and because the tenant’s purchase right arose after a long period.
The respondent also claimed equity and had obtained an order permitting purchase as a tenant.
The Court found the equities claimed by the parties to be equal.
issues.conclusion: The respondent’s right to purchase prevailed, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the maxim “in aequali jure, melior est conditio possidentis”: where rights and equities are equal, the law should prevail and the loss should lie where it falls. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this equitable maxim in the judgment.

rule.if: tenant_purchase_appeal and both_parties_claim_equity and equities_are_equal and tenant_has_an_established_purchase_right

predicates.tenant_purchase_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning a tenant’s right to purchase land.
predicates.both_parties_claim_equity: Both the landholder and the tenant rely on equitable considerations.
predicates.equities_are_equal: The court finds that neither party’s equitable claim outweighs the other’s.
predicates.tenant_has_an_established_purchase_right: The tenant has a purchase right that remains effective under the applicable law.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning a tenant’s purchase right, when both parties claim equity, the court finds their equities equal, and the tenant has an established purchase right, that right prevails.
